thesis.core: Shenzhen Airport owns scarce aviation infrastructure and generates substantial operating cash, but reported 2026 profit growth is dominated by nonrecurring gains rather than durable aviation operating returns. The current share price implies a premium to book while normalized attributable ROE remains around 4-5%, leaving insufficient risk-adjusted upside.
thesis.variant_wedge: 9M attributable profit rose 91.80% to RMB897.83m, but deducted profit rose only 0.23% to RMB403.63m; nonrecurring items RMB494.20m account for about 55% of reported attributable profit, including large asset disposals. 9M CFO RMB1.77bn is real but not identical to owner-distributable FCF after lease obligations, financing and airport renewal capex.
thesis.normalized_earnings_basis: Use 2026 nine-month deducted attributable profit RMB403.63m annualized as a rough RMB538.18m (~RMB0.262/share) recurring-earnings cross-check, not reported RMB897.83m annualized. 2026Q3 parent equity RMB12.199bn gives BVPS about RMB5.95. Underwrite recurring ROE around 4.4% before any sustained passenger/retail profit improvement.

operating_and_financial_quality.judgment: Balance sheet has liquidity and operating cash generation; infrastructure quality is real. However earnings quality fails the defensive-return test: nonrecurring gains explain most of reported profit growth, while underlying deducted earnings are flat. The 2026Q3 report describes acquisition-related remeasurement investment income and fund exits. Current ROE after stripping nonrecurring gains does not support premium-to-book valuation without a credible recurring margin step-up.

normalized_earnings_basis.rationale: P/B scenarios reflect scarce airport infrastructure, liquidity, and recurring ROE below typical equity cost of capital; price targets exclude future dividends and one-off gains.

catalysts: Sustained increase in passenger, aircraft and high-margin non-aeronautical revenue with recurring deducted profit growth.
Two or more quarters of stronger recurring ROE supported by cash generation after maintenance and lease obligations.
Transparent cash distribution and disciplined airport infrastructure capex improve shareholder economics.
kill_thesis: Recurring deducted profit fails to improve despite traffic recovery and higher reported revenue.
Material airport lease, concession or capital expenditure commitments erode owner-distributable cash.
Reported profit growth continues to depend on asset disposals, investment fair-value remeasurement or other nonrecurring items.
Adverse traffic, tariff regulation, retail concession or related-party cost changes reduce normalized returns.
